notes:
ACCESS: Claude-in-Chrome connector only, one dedicated tab, no HTTP/proxy route used. robots.txt was read in that tab: it names no Claude/anthropic/ClaudeBot agent at all, only a generic User-agent:* block covering /account/, /checkout/, /bin/ and similar, so all category listings are allowed. No Akamai challenge appeared in a real browser session (the prior Home-Decor pass was 403-walled on every HTTP route). TREE: built from (a) the Furniture mega-menu embedded in every page's HTML, (b) each department hub's own 'plp-subway-carousel' child list, and (c) the site's unprotected /assets/sitemap-supercategory-and-spategory.xml (173 hub URLs) and /assets/sitemap-plp.xml (1852 listing URLs). Everything was retrieved with same-origin fetch() run via javascript_tool inside the loaded crateandbarrel.com tab, paced ~4-6s apart; nothing was fetched from outside the browser. Where a node's placement was doubtful its parent was confirmed from the page's own JSON-LD BreadcrumbList. COUNTS: the rendered listing header
N Items
. On every one of the ~60 pages fetched it was identical to the container attribute data-num-results, so evidence quotes both. Two exhaustion checks prove the number is exact rather than a facet estimate: Benches data-num-results=15 with exactly 15 unique digitalData productId entries, and Game Tables 11 with exactly 11. Pagination sanity check: /furniture/sectional-sofas/2 still reports 728 and serves a different set of 100 products, while /kids/kids-dressers/2 returns the identical 100 products as page 1 - so the round 100 for Kids Dressers is that category's true total, not a page cap. Second reads of Sofas (122), Dining Room Tables (61) and Kids Dressers (100) matched the first read exactly. Constructor.io was deliberately NOT used as a count source: the prior pass on this site and a sibling worker on CB2 both proved it disagrees with the PLP header on this platform. ALIASES COLLAPSED (identical h1 and identical count, i.e. one node served under two slugs): /furniture/coffee-table|console-table|end-table/1 are the singular aliases of the plural /coffee-tables|console-tables|end-tables/1; /furniture/poufs/1 serves 'Ottomans & Storage Cubes' (105); /outdoor-furniture/outdoor-adirondack-chairs/1 serves 'Outdoor Lounge & Swivel Chairs' (97); /outdoor-furniture/master-the-mix/1 serves 'Outdoor Lounge & Dining Sets' (9); /furniture/bookcases/1 = /furniture/bookcases-and-shelves/1 (51); /furniture/entryway-floating-shelves/1 = /furniture/floating-shelves/1 (8); /furniture/kids-beds/1 = /kids/beds/1 (132); /furniture/kids-desks-and-desk-chairs/1 = /kids/desks-chairs/1 (78); /furniture/cribs-and-bassinets/1 = /kids/cribs-bassinets/1 (105); each /kids/all-*-furniture/1 = its matching Crate&kids hub. NOT an alias, verified by product-ID diff: /kids/nightstands/1 and /furniture/nightstands/1 both report 50 but share ZERO product IDs - two genuinely different catalogues, so both are kept. GROUPING ROWS: Living Room, Ottomans & Benches, TV Stands & Media Consoles, Coffee & Accent Tables, Dining Room & Kitchen, Bedroom, Storage & Modular, Home Office, Entryway, Bathroom Furniture, Baby & Kids Furniture with its four room hubs, and the two Outdoor hubs - none of these is also recorded as a leaf. EXCLUDED and why: Mattresses & Box Springs (/furniture/mattresses-foundations/1), /kids/kids-mattresses/1 and /kids/crib-mattresses/1 - bedding, not furniture. Floating Shelves (8) - the site's own breadcrumb files it under 'Home > Decor & Pillows > Organization', i.e. wall shelving, not furniture. Bath Storage (/furniture/bathroom-storage/1, 57) - product tiles inspected and they are bath accessories, totes, canisters, laundry baskets, shower caddies and toilet-paper holders. Bathroom Hardware, Bath Faucets, Bath Lighting and Bath Mirrors under the /bath/bath-furniture/ hub. Kids Toy Boxes & Storage (59) and Storage Bins & Baskets - standalone storage goods. Kids Wall Shelves & Hooks (/kids/shelving-hardware/1, 68) - wall shelves plus hardware. Office Accessories, Entryway Decor, Patio Umbrellas, Patio Furniture Covers, Fire Pits & Tables, Outdoor Cushions, Outdoor Decor, and the whole Outdoor Kitchen & Entertaining hub (its seven children are melamine dinnerware, acrylic drinkware, beverage tubs, grills, pizza ovens, BBQ tools and picnic gear). Per section 3: every *-collection PLP (Petrie, Lounge, Gather, Cavett and the 60+ /furniture-sectional-sofas//1 pages), 'Sofa & Sectional Collections', Outdoor Furniture Collections, Best Sellers, New Furniture, In-Stock, Clearance, Sale, Custom Furniture, Replacement Slipcovers, Made in USA, buying guides, and every style or material filter page (Leather, Italian, Scandinavian, Rustic, Art Deco, Marble, Velvet, Wicker, Metal, Teak, Polywood). KNOWN OVERLAP: Crate & Barrel publishes a room tree and a product-type tree over the same catalogue, so e.g. Coffee Tables appears in both the Living Room and the Coffee & Accent Tables carousels; each node is emitted exactly once, under the parent its breadcrumb names. Crate&kids is a separate department whose rows do not overlap the main-site rows.
